brief: Goldman's chart pack argues equity markets are rotating into Quality amid an AI unwind. US Quality is at 12-month highs, a flight to quality Goldman ties to higher rates being priced in; Quality works when earnings momentum weakens, and its valuation premium to the market is now below the recent-years norm. In Europe, Quality had underperformed for a few years, though one chart shows it gaining ground since September 1 while another shows it still lagging the market recently. Separately, Goldman's prime brokerage data shows global AI stocks saw the second-largest net selling in the past year, net allocation to global AI stocks fell to 26.1% of total single-stock net from about 33% in June, and the aggregate long/short ratio dropped to 3.27 from a June peak of 4.34; the S&P 500 ex-AI has rallied as AI names and the Momentum factor sold off. High-yield spreads have widened for AI-related issuers, and Goldman expects the AI capex earnings boost to fade. US equity multiples have fallen as yields rose, though balance sheets face limited risk since interest expense is manageable and coverage ratios are historically high; the market has also downgraded its growth outlook, visible in cyclicals lagging defensives.
